events.description: Summer Sports Experience is an instructional youth program that teaches sports skills. events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. events.description: NYRR Open Run brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.St. Mary's Park offers a wonderful respite from the hustle and bustle of urban life. Located in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx, the park features rolling hills, expanses of green grass, and grand old trees. The site was once part of the estate of Jonas Bronck (1600-43), for whom the Bronx is named. It is one of the largest parks in the area with a pool, playground, basketball courts, an indoor recreation center, picnic seating areas, and more. In the winter, the hills are perfect for sledding. St. Mary’s Park received $30 million from NYC’s Anchor Parks initiative, which will renovate the park’s ballfields, pathways, and amphitheater.

events.description: Join historian Terrell L. Armistead in a special tour along the Bronx River at River Park as they share the ecological stories and community histories of the Bronx River. Led in honor of Morgan Powell, a founding member of the Bronx River Restoration and a passionate advocate for the reclamation of the Bronx River. His research has been fundamental in sharing the lesser known histories of Black and Brown Bronxites and their contributions to the eco-cultural history of NYC. events.title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
events.description: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.

events.title: In the Distortion of Celestial Privacy, a Door Left Open in the Mind
events.description: Set within the living landscape of 6BC Botanical Garden, this third annual iteration, curated by Sarah Viviana Valdez, brings together the sculptural practices of Ori Carlin, Erin Lingard, and Lizzy Chemel. The artists span materials and techniques, notably including wood-fired ceramics, metal, concrete, salvaged materials and stained glass mirages. Their works share a common sentiment toward incredible craftsmanship deriving from botany, memory, and family histories. Throughout the garden's labyrinth, each location and placement of these pieces will similarly act as an embroidery unifying the rhythms and quiet transformations to shape their own narratives. Beginning in the afternoon and unfolding toward sundown, the exhibition will culminate with closing performances by Sky Axe, Karol Konstancia with ensemble, and Fillan Fernando. These performers honor traditions of myth, folklore, songwriting, choral a cappella, and poetry. The intent is to offer gifts that extend the exhibition’s exploration of memory and storytelling. We invite visitors to wander through a space where sculpture, sound, and movement become small openings into remembrance and shared imagination. For folks who feel compelled, the curator will offer tours throughout the day. Enjoy these presented moments of pause where the private worlds we carry within us are invited to briefly open onto the garden and one another.

events.description: Celebrate National Dance Day with a guided walk through Fort Tryon Park featuring dance, live music & poetry!Meet at Broadway and Dongan Place Entrance at 3PM | Audience Members Guided Through the Park On Wheelchair Accessible Pathways | Walking ProductionCelebrate National Dance Day with an immersive, multi-disciplinary arts production in Fort Tryon Park!
